experiment: learning-v2b model run 4: precision arms (4a crease-position imitation, 4b bigger network)
predeclared: 2026-11-05, after run 3 (precision is the bottleneck; the model fits only about 48% of its own training data), before any run-4 training
examples: one example per (request, fold budget) reference answer; train split for fitting, validation split for checkpoint selection, test split evaluated once at the end

inputs.note: box length and height are sorted because a box and its swapped partner are the same problem (D30); box width and sheet width only decide feasibility and are not inputs

outputs.foldCount: 12-way classification (0..11 folds), restricted to at most the budget at prediction time
outputs.panels: 11 stick-breaking fractions in [0, 1] (each panel at least 5% of sheet length); the first (folds) are used
outputs.angles: 11 values in [0, 1] mapped to 1..180 degrees; the first (folds) are used
outputs.placement: not predicted: the predicted shape is placed with the same deterministic placement search as the reference (wall placement)

loss: imitation (as run 1) + 100 x fitLoss + weight x tighterPenalty
checkpointSelection: every 50 epochs: validation pass rate from the Node reference checker (valid + fits after placement, 721 motion states); best pass rate wins, ties broken by lower validation loss; stop after 600 epochs without improvement
successCriterion: D20: share of test (request, budget) answers whose predicted design passes all hard rules; the user judges a visual sample. Reference point 95%.
reportedAlongside: all creases on walls (D34) and opening angle relative to the reference answer
fold count equal to the reference
baselines on the same test answers: hand rule (fold-budget-agnostic), nearest-neighbour copy of the closest training answer with the same budget, reference solver
test answers needing more folds than any training answer reported separately (known split imbalance)
ceiling: Decoded reference labels (perfect imitation) pass 4,343/4,359 training answers (99.6%); the 16 failures are zero-slack fits that tip over by floating-point decoding error. This is the ceiling for imitation in this output format.
changeFromRun1: adds a differentiable fit penalty; everything else (data, inputs, outputs, model, optimizer, imitation loss, checkpoint rule) is unchanged

fitLoss.definition: fold the predicted shape in PyTorch (true fold count, predicted panels and angles), turn it by the reference answer's placement angle, and penalise squared overshoot of its side-view extents beyond (1 - margin) x the usable box, in sheet-length units
fitLoss.note: training target only; rules and checker unchanged

changeFromRun2: fit penalty fixed at weight 100 (run-2 choice); adds a one-sided angle penalty; everything else unchanged

tighterPenalty.definition: for each used fold: squared amount by which the predicted fold angle exceeds (is more closed than) the reference angle, in the normalized angle units used by imitation, averaged over used folds

runSelection: no selection between arms; both reported. Judged first on training-set pass rate and scatter (can it fit precisely?), then validation pass, bias and scatter, tolerance curve.
reportedPerRun: fold-angle, panel-length and opening-angle bias and scatter (scripts/precision-report.py)
changeFromRun3: two separate arms, each changing one thing from run 3 (t100): 4a replaces parameter imitation (panel and angle MSE) with crease-position imitation; 4b uses hidden layers [512, 512, 512]

4a.imitation: fold-count cross-entropy + 10 x mean squared distance between corresponding side-view vertices (first panel fixed, unrotated) of the predicted and reference shapes, in sheet-length units, using the true fold count
